answer.original_source: NN, Inc. (company announcement as reported by finance.yahoo.com; no separate NVIDIA source in the supplied records)
answer.new_information: Reported late June 2026 (publication 2026-07-01): NN, Inc. announced adding 47 machine centers for liquid cooling production at its Wuxi, China plant for NVIDIA AI data center racks. Per the company statement relayed in the record, 100% of the new capacity was pre-sold under multi-year, multi-product awards, and NN targeted US$80-US$90 million of accretive new business in 2026. The record also reports NN's removal from the Russell Microcap Value Index in late June 2026 and third-party narrative/analyst revenue and earnings projections for NN to 2028. These are NN-level facts, party targets and third-party estimates, not NVIDIA disclosures. The NVIDIA link is NN's characterization of its end market; the record names no NVIDIA contract, purchase order or NVIDIA statement. The NN revenue and earnings projections are not NVIDIA revenue or backlog.
answer.reason: The incoming claim concerns NN, Inc., which is not the covered company (NVDA). Its relevance to NVDA would be as a supplier in NVIDIA's rack supply chain, but the record does not establish a direct NVIDIA purchase commitment, and the $80-US$90 million figure is NN's own 2026 target for new business, not NVIDIA revenue or NVIDIA order data. The supplier's revenue, backlog or pre-sold capacity cannot be treated as NVDA orders or revenue. The NN Russell index removal and analyst projections have no business connection to NVDA. No catalog or stored question exists for NVDA, so no existing argument is changed and no new NVDA question is supported by this record.
answer.independent_judgement: The incoming record is an NN-focused commentary built on a company announcement relayed by a media outlet. The independent origin is NN, Inc. for the capacity and 2026 target claims. For the covered NVDA business, the NN expansion at most offers a conditional supply-chain signal: if NVIDIA is confirmed as a customer for the Wuxi capacity, it would indicate continued liquid-cooling rack supply sourcing outside NVIDIA's direct books. That link is unconfirmed here, and the record provides no NVDA-side figures, customer disclosures or capacity data to test it. The rest of the article (dividend, quantum computing and fair value promotional content) carries no research conclusion. Treat as background only.
